desc: Ten orange orb-shaped lights were reported from the A1 north of Darlington. A local astronomer suggested such sightings are usually balloons or lanterns.
place: A1(M) north of Darlington, County Durham
title: A1 Darlington orange orbs

desc: On 12 January 2008 a driver and passenger saw a tall man in a grey coat by the road with a featureless, faintly glowing oval head.
title: A470 faceless figure, Llyswen

desc: A mechanic and three friends saw a low round object trailing flames pass over their car and disappear over the sea, and the coastguard took calls about bright lights offshore. A meteor was suggested but not confirmed.
title: A55 flaming object over Llandudno

desc: Two men driving the A70 reported a two-tiered disc over the road that released a curtain of light, after which they found hours unaccounted for; under hypnosis they described an abduction. No explanation was given.
place: A70 near Harperrig Reservoir, West Lothian
title: A70 Harperrig abduction

desc: In 1962 brothers Derek and Norman Ferguson reported a series of figures and animals that vanished as they drove at night, while their car rocked; other drivers reported phantom pedestrians in 1957, 1995 and 1997.
place: A75 Kinmount Straight, near Annan, Dumfries and Galloway
title: A75 Kinmount Straight

desc: Staff at the medieval merchant's house report being prodded in the loft, the smell of flowers, rattling and slamming doors, and display plates moving overnight. A woman by the loft fireplace and a Victorian man in the corridor are also described.
title: Aberconwy House prodding and moving plates

desc: A retired police officer reported fragmented white lights drifting over the town over several days, including one display lasting about ten minutes. No explanation was given.
title: Abergele drifting lights

desc: Guests describe figures in naval dress, a figure hanging at a Crosby Room window and a ghost called George, with most reports from the third floor.
place: The Adelphi Hotel, Ranelagh Place, Liverpool
title: Adelphi Hotel third floor

desc: The 15th-century poet Lewys Glyn Cothi placed the Afanc, a Welsh water monster, in Llyn Syfaddon. Other traditions link it to Llyn Barfog and a pool near Betws-y-Coed.
title: Afanc of Llyn Syfaddon

desc: A child and father reported two small lights moving around each other, prompting a letter to the MoD. The ministry replied that it had no evidence of life beyond Earth and gave no explanation.
title: Altrincham dancing lights letter

desc: Mountaineer J. Norman Collie said he fled the summit in 1891 after hearing giant crunching footsteps behind him in mist. Later climbers reported a looming figure; explanations include the Brocken spectre and fatigue.
title: Am Fear Liath Mor, Ben Macdui

desc: Billed by its owners as the most haunted building in England with around twenty ghosts, it became a paranormal event venue after conversion to a guesthouse in 1968.
title: Ancient Ram Inn

desc: Anne Boleyn is said to lead a procession to the Chapel of St Peter ad Vincula; in 1864 a sentry bayoneted a white figure outside the King's House and was cleared after two witnesses backed him.
place: Tower Green, Tower of London, London
title: Anne Boleyn and Tower Green

desc: A Haunted St Helens investigator says a friend's photo on the staircase of the derelict mansion-pub caught a figure passing between the banisters. She insists no mark on the wall explains it.
place: Former Crying Tree, Grange Lane, Gateacre
title: Apparition snapped at the old Crying Tree, Gateacre

desc: A cable layer said his car stalled near a large Toblerone-shaped object. Police timings were found to conflict with his account.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Armadale Toblerone and stalled car

desc: At the site of the 1691 battle, where Jacobite dead were left unburied, visitors report hearing screams.
title: Aughrim battlefield screams

desc: A family drove into a green mist and arrived home with about three hours missing.
title: Aveley abduction

desc: A brightly coloured object hovering about 100 m up was reported in Preston, with a similar report from Wigan at about the same time. No explanation was given.
title: Avenham Park coloured object

desc: Record-breaking pilot Tom Campbell Black died in a runway accident at Speke in 1936, and his shadowy form is reported around the old hangars.
title: Aviator Tom Campbell Black at Speke airfield

desc: The castle hotel is reputed to be one of Ulster's most haunted places and keeps a 'Ghost Room'.
place: Ballygally Castle, Coast Road, Ballygally, Co Antrim
title: Ballygally Castle

desc: Knocking and flying furniture in a Glasgow home involved police, housing officials, clergy and investigator Archie Roy; it faded when a teenage boy at its centre left school.
title: Balornock Poltergeist

desc: Four separate UFO reports were made over County Down. The official investigation traced the lights to lasers on the roof of a Bangor hotel.
title: Bangor hotel laser 'UFO'

desc: A spectral black dog with huge eyes is said to haunt this limestone gorge; an 1830 ballad tells of a man found dead after trying to summon it.
title: Barguest of Trollers Gill

desc: A silver-suited humanoid was reported standing beside a craft at a road junction in the village. The claim was not verified.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Barnston silver humanoid

desc: Volunteers and staff at the 1840s Masonic hall describe shadows, noises and a feeling of being watched in the basement, and visitors hear furniture dragged upstairs. Ghost-hunt bookings now help fund the building and Most Haunted filmed there.
title: Basement presence at Clifton Hall, Birkenhead

desc: Staff report being touched and objects flying, with a boy called Billy and a grey lady said to be a woman hanged as a witch.
place: The Bate Hall, Chestergate, Macclesfield, Cheshire
title: Bate Hall, Macclesfield

desc: From 2 February to 27 March 1834 the servants' bells rang violently with no one touching them, witnessed by Major Edward Moor FRS, his son and servants; no cause was found.
title: Bealings Bells

desc: In spring 1964 a woman walking in the castle grounds found her dog cowering in a beam of light coming down from the sky. When she picked the dog up, her arm was burned and its fur was singed. Neither suffered lasting harm.
title: Beam of light burns woman at Denbigh Castle

desc: A farmer shot an animal blamed for killing lambs; it turned out to be an escaped pet lemur.
title: Beast of Bala shot, Llanuwchllyn

desc: Police and vets captured a young female Eurasian lynx after a chase across school playing fields. Named Lara, she went to London Zoo and later to a zoo in France.
title: Beast of Barnet lynx captured, Cricklewood

desc: The laird of Pitcaple Castle blamed a panther-like animal for partly eaten lambs near Whiteford, with large prints seen in snow, and a bailiff reported a long black cat at Pitcaple Bridge.
title: Beast of Bennachie lambs and prints, Pitcaple

desc: Twelve sheep were killed around Pontrhydfendigaid in June 1981, and government vets reportedly judged the killer stronger than a fox or dog. Further killings in the mid-1990s and around Ponterwyd in 2012 were blamed on the same 'beast'.
title: Beast of Bont sheep killings

desc: A Ceredigion farmer whose ewes were killed said a police officer told him big cats winter in Brechfa Forest and summer in Myherin Forest near Devil's Bridge. Police disputed his account and no evidence was produced.
title: Beast of Brechfa migration claim

desc: Twenty-two sightings of a big cat were logged in rural Buchan between May 2000 and January 2002, and local MP Alex Salmond raised livestock attacks in the House of Commons. No hard evidence was found.
title: Beast of Buchan

desc: Decades of Dartmoor big cat sightings and livestock deaths were later linked to pumas reportedly released by animal trainer Mary Chipperfield when her Plymouth zoo closed in 1978.
title: Beast of Dartmoor puma release

desc: A South Molton farmer claimed more than 100 sheep killed in three months, prompting a newspaper reward and a Royal Marines sniper deployment. No cat was found and the deaths are now attributed to large dogs.
title: Beast of Exmoor sheep losses

desc: A man running at night with his dog said a five-to-six-foot cheetah-like animal stared at him and then chased them through the wood before giving up.
title: Beast of Sydenham chases runner

desc: Visitors describe footsteps, cold spots, whistling and jangling keys attributed to a jailer, and dread in the execution room. Local lore says a man hanged in 1862 cursed the church clock so its faces never agree.
title: Beaumaris Gaol jailer and clock curse

desc: A farming couple said they had seen a puma near their home, took plaster casts of paw prints and blamed big cats for livestock losses. The wife said the animal left her alone when she met it by the garden.
title: Beddgelert farmers' puma and paw casts

desc: A driver reported a flat disc passing over her car, dimming its lights and cutting out the engine and radio; an 11-year-old also saw it. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Belcher's Bar car stall

desc: MoD papers released by the National Archives cover an investigation into a reported UFO near the airport. The released summary gives no explanation.
source: The National Archives – UFO files highlights (March 2009)
title: Belfast Airport UFO investigation

desc: A caller reported a silent object with flashing green and red lights rising from behind their house and flying towards the docks. No explanation was recorded.
title: Belfast silent rising object

desc: The tower house is said to be haunted by a faceless Lady Margaret Hardnett searching mirrors for her reflection and by a shipwrecked Spanish minstrel.
place: Belvelly Castle, near Cobh, Co Cork
title: Belvelly Castle mirrors

desc: The 'pauper's ghost' is linked to the workhouse that once stood here; in one 1970s account a man met a stranger whose head flopped back on a broken neck. A medium said Bernie died falling from a workhouse window.
title: Bernie Brown on the Metropolitan Cathedral steps

desc: A loud bang and tremor felt across North Wales, with lights seen on the mountain. Officially put down to an earthquake and poachers' lamps or meteors. Often called the 'Welsh Roswell'.
title: Berwyn Mountain incident

desc: Around 30 people reported a saucer roughly 30 ft wide hovering over a residential street in daylight, with car engines said to have stalled. No explanation was recorded.
place: King Harold's Way, Bexleyheath, Greater London
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Bexleyheath hovering saucer

desc: At about 8.30am a dog walker saw a slender, short-haired animal with a bushy tail, bigger than her spaniel, staring at her from six to eight feet away across a fence. It ran into bushes when her dog approached.
title: Big cat by Whitby Park tennis courts

desc: A passer-by filmed a dark animal estimated at four to five feet long sitting in a field before it vanished behind a hill. A sheep had been found badly torn apart nearby.
title: Big cat filmed after sheep killed, Askrigg

desc: A man crossing the course at about 8pm saw a large black animal near one of the holes. He said he nearly passed out at the size of it.
title: Big cat on Old Colwyn golf course

desc: Police were told of a big cat, variously suggested as a puma or larger cat, roaming close to the village at the foot of Snowdon.
title: Big cat roaming near Llanberis

desc: A black big cat nicknamed the Black Beast of Ossett was reported in the Coxley Valley in 2000.
title: Black Beast of Ossett

desc: A nun is said to walk through the building, guests report a crying child that stops when spoken to, and a man has been seen in the bar.
place: Black Boy Inn, Northgate Street, Caernarfon, Gwynedd
title: Black Boy Inn nun, Caernarfon

desc: A smallholder reported seeing a large black cat twice within about two days, and one of her yearling ewes was found eviscerated.
title: Black cat and eviscerated ewe, Penuwch

desc: A walker filmed a large black cat running across a lane in front of him. Weeks later a villager watched a dog-sized black cat sprint across a field near the same spot.
title: Black cat filmed on lane, Pontybodkin

desc: At about 7.30am a dog walker saw a very large jet-black cat with a round head and pointed ears staring at her from about 50 yards away. It fled when her dog noticed it. Police later reported four sheep killed nearby that day.
title: Black cat in Nercwys Forest above Mold

desc: Several workers saw a muscular black cat about three feet long pass close by in woodland at lunchtime; a police patrol searched without finding it.
title: Black cat near Cannock Chase Enterprise Centre

desc: A couple driving near the Premier Inn roundabout saw a large black cat stalking sheep; it slipped behind a bush and was gone when they looped back.
title: Black cat stalking sheep, Holyhead

desc: A motorist driving at 45-50 mph after dark saw a large black cat-like animal dart across a junction.
title: Black feline crosses Nercwys road junction

desc: A woman in black with a black dog was said to cross the Dee marsh at night, a tale perhaps spread by smugglers to keep people away.
place: Marsh between Burton and the Harp Inn, Neston
title: Black lady and dog on Burton Marsh

desc: North Wales Police logged a report of a black leopard about 4 ft long in the Mold area. Officers investigated but saw nothing.
title: Black leopard reported near Mold

desc: The Pritchard family reported a violent poltergeist nicknamed Fred that threw objects, made puddles and allegedly dragged their daughter up the stairs; the case was popularised by Colin Wilson in 1981.
place: 30 East Drive, Chequerfield, Pontefract, West Yorkshire
title: Black Monk of Pontefract

desc: A witness told police they had seen a black panther moving through hedgerows and insisted it was not a large dog. Officers found nothing.
title: Black panther in hedges, Llandudno

desc: Several dog walkers saw a jet-black cat with pointed ears and a long tail bolt into a field near the nature reserve.
title: Black panther near Brickfield Pond, Rhyl

desc: A morning walker reported a black panther with yellow eyes running along the railway tracks near Barkby Bridge.
title: Black panther on rail line, Barkby, Prestatyn

desc: A large black panther-type cat was reported running along a road. Officers visited the area but saw nothing.
title: Black panther running along road, Caernarfon

desc: At dusk a man saw a large black cat creeping low through grass towards sheep behind the Queen's Head pub. He took two phone photos, but the animal had gone when he looked up.
title: Black puma stalking sheep at Glanwydden

desc: During a violent storm a black dog was said to have run through St Mary's church, killing two worshippers. The same day it was reported at Blythburgh church, where scorch marks on the door are attributed to it.
title: Black Shuck at Bungay church

desc: A UFO was reported above Blackpool pier and logged by the MoD UFO desk. No explanation was recorded.
source: The National Archives – UFO files highlights (2013)
title: Blackpool pier UFO report

desc: A couple reported a UFO hovering over their garden and later visits from a group of men dressed in black. No explanation was given.
title: Blairgowrie garden UFO and men in black

desc: Linked to a fatal crash in November 1965, drivers have reported a young woman who vanishes from their car or is hit and never found, including accounts from 1971 and 1972.
place: A229 Blue Bell Hill, near Aylesford, Kent
title: Blue Bell Hill hitchhiker

desc: A brilliant blue light crossed Wales and was seen from the south up to Anglesey. A Rhos Point fisherman said it lit the whole sky over Colwyn Bay and Llandudno for several seconds. The RAF said it was not an aircraft, and a meteor was suggested.
title: Blue light over Colwyn Bay and Llandudno

desc: A lady in a blue dress is said to walk the sculpture gallery and pass through a wall, and children are heard playing in the toy room. A security guard reported seeing only a pair of legs in buckled shoes and white stockings.
title: Bodelwyddan Castle Blue Lady

desc: Repeated sightings of a large black cat and livestock kills. A 1995 government study found no proof.
title: Beast of Bodmin Moor

desc: Several people report stepping briefly into a 1950s or earlier version of the street.
title: Bold Street time slips

desc: An older woman in black with a bonnet appeared on the road and suddenly vanished; a newspaper said cyclists braked hard to avoid her. Others saw a small ball of fire that quickly disappeared.
title: Bonneted lady on Woodchurch Road

desc: Area with thousands of reported sightings since the early 1990s, dubbed the Falkirk Triangle.
title: Bonnybridge sightings

desc: A resident filmed a luminous pink object for several minutes and other villagers reported lights. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – List of reported UFO sightings
title: Bonsall pink object filmed

desc: Once called the most haunted house in England. A nun, a phantom coach and wall writings were reported. The rectory burned down in 1939.
title: Borley Rectory

desc: Campers at the west end of the loch watched an object about the bulk of a small cow cross the bay at 4am, leaving a large bow wave.
title: Bow wave crossing Loch Arkaig

desc: Anomalous photographs of a humped shape in Windermere in 2011 led to the nickname Bownessie. Sceptics noted similar images have turned out to be floating debris.
title: Bownessie photographs, Windermere

desc: An 11-year-old searching for his lost cat was left with claw marks on his cheek and police issued a big cat warning. A police helicopter search found nothing.
title: Boy scratched by 'big cat', Trellech

desc: A silvery-blue dart or sphere was photographed over Braddan in daylight, and an off-duty police officer said they saw something at the same time. No explanation was given.
title: Braddan silvery-blue dart

desc: Phantom war horses and hoofbeats are reported in the park and linked locally to the Battle of Bramham Moor in 1408.
place: Bramham Park, Bramham, Leeds, West Yorkshire
title: Bramham Park phantom horses

desc: A local man reported a winged, dog-like creature over Braemar Road in summer 1984 and again in 1985, and others described a large black bird-like shape on the gasometer. Much of the testimony is now regarded as hoax or media-driven.
title: Brentford Griffin

desc: Around 7am, people in Wrexham, Brymbo, Rhos, Garden Village and Minera reported a bright light moving across the sky, then a bright flash about a minute later. No cause was confirmed.
title: Bright light and flash over Wrexham

desc: Phantom monks are said to inhabit the inn, with monk-like shadows seen in the public rooms.
place: Britannia Inn, Horseshoe Pass, Llangollen, Denbighshire
title: Britannia Inn monks, Horseshoe Pass

desc: A dome-shaped object with an apparent door was watched hovering for about an hour and was logged by the Berry Head coastguard. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Brixham domed object

desc: Fourteen schoolchildren described a silver cigar-shaped craft landing in a field and a figure in a silver suit. Part of the 'Dyfed Triangle' wave.
title: Broad Haven school sighting

desc: A pale man with his head lolling on his shoulder has been seen in the dressing rooms since the 1920s and is said to herald misfortune. In February 1993 a staging of The Devil Rides Out was reportedly plagued by disturbances after a pentagram was chalked on stage.
title: Broken-neck man in the Epstein Theatre

desc: In the early 1970s two men in a car saw a figure in a brown habit step out in front of them, and the driver braked hard, but nothing was found. Readers linked it to a monk-like ghost near Holywell and a misty figure on Halkyn Mountain.
title: Brown-habited figure on the A5123 at Halkyn

desc: Sightings date from 1835, and on 19 September 1936 Country Life photographers captured a veiled figure on the staircase; sceptics suggest double exposure.
title: Brown Lady of Raynham Hall

desc: Staff and guests report a monk said to have died in a fall and a young motorcyclist killed nearby, along with shadows, cold spots and a woman's figure.
place: The Bull, Chapel Street, Abergele, Conwy
title: Bull Hotel monk, Abergele

desc: A taxi driver and passenger watched a silent silver cigar with a pulsing light hover, change shape and move back and forth for about three minutes. No explanation was given.
title: Burnley silver cigar

desc: Driving to work at 3.45am, a bus driver watched a monk cross in front of his car and vanish; he later heard the area was said to be haunted by a monk and nun.
title: Bus driver's vanishing monk, Walton

desc: A witness reported a green, star-like object with red on one side that looked as if it would hit their house. It was logged in MoD files without explanation.
title: Caernarfon green object

desc: Photo of a large diamond-shaped object hovering above the hills with a jet nearby. The image was released in full in 2022.
title: Calvine photograph

desc: Police shot a loose wild cat, reported as a caracal though a police report called it a lynx.
title: Caracal shot by police, Fintona

desc: Two teachers watched a silent silver cone-shaped object about 100 m up for around five minutes before it vanished. A local monitor speculated about a spy plane.
title: Carlisle silver cone

desc: A slow-moving object was watched for about half an hour travelling east to west and repeatedly retracing its path; witnesses ruled out an aircraft. No explanation was given.
title: Carrickmacross retracing object

desc: The hotel is said to be haunted by an angry chambermaid whose last wish was ignored, and guests report a phantom cat climbing onto beds at night.
title: Castle Hotel chambermaid, Conwy

desc: Reports include a lady in green near the Dickens Bar and twin girls seen at the foot of beds.
place: Castle Mona, Douglas, Isle of Man
title: Castle Mona green lady

desc: The 14th-century castle, scene of many executions, has reports of shadowy figures, a White Lady and a Woman in Black.
place: Castle Rushen, Castletown, Isle of Man
title: Castle Rushen White Lady

desc: Legend says Catherine Howard broke from her guards in 1541 and ran along the gallery to plead with Henry VIII; it has since been called the Haunted Gallery.
place: Haunted Gallery, Hampton Court Palace, London
title: Catherine Howard, Hampton Court

desc: After a crash at Fiveways while rushing his pregnant wife to hospital, a man woke to be told his wife and three children had never existed. Tom Slemen calls it one of his strangest cases; names were changed.
title: Childwall man whose family never existed

desc: Legend tells of a cave near the castle entrance that draws in anyone who comes within five paces. A fiddler who walked in playing one Halloween never came out, and a fox fled out smelling of brimstone.
title: Chirk Castle cave of no return

desc: Three ghosts, including a Civil War cavalier and the original owner's father, are said to haunt the 16th-century house, where objects move; it was investigated in 2007.
place: Churche's Mansion, Hospital Street, Nantwich, Cheshire
title: Churche's Mansion, Nantwich

desc: Two brothers visiting family saw a circular object heading towards the Berwyns, then a brighter, oddly flashing light over the far side of the lake that climbed quickly. A Llanuwchllyn family reported orange circular objects over the mountains.
title: Circular object and light over Llyn Tegid

desc: A large glassy sphere was watched over the coast for more than an hour and reportedly painted on radar at RAF Manby, departing as RAF aircraft approached. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Cleethorpes glass sphere tracked by RAF Manby

desc: Two oval orbs were seen and photographed; conventional aircraft were said to have been ruled out. No identification was offered.
title: Clifden oval orbs photographed

desc: The Welsh Federation of Independent Ufologists recorded a cluster of UFO reports around the Clwydian Range, Prestatyn, Meliden and Dyserth in 1985 and 1986.
title: Clwydian Range UFO flap

desc: A Victorian boy crushed by a coal delivery is said to haunt the mansion; staff describe sickness after taunting him and footsteps along a corridor at night. The cellar is now sealed.
title: Coal-cellar boy of Calderstones House

desc: Windows along the street were smashed by flying lumps of coal, and the breakages carried on even after police began patrolling.
title: Coal-throwing outbreak, Myers Street

desc: A long-exposure photograph of the library taken in 1891, while Lord Combermere's funeral was under way, appears to show a figure in his chair.
title: Combermere Abbey ghost photo

desc: Two police officers reported a domed object about 100 ft across with lit portholes near the A629. No explanation was recorded.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Cononley police domed craft

desc: A huge arrowhead-shaped object, described as the size of ten football pitches, was reported. A local astronomer argued such sightings can usually be explained, but none was given for this case.
title: Corbridge giant arrowhead

desc: A patch of scrub next to Liverpool's oldest church is said to be protected by an old promise never to build on it. Tales describe coloured orbs ('corpse candles'), 'black goblins' and a dark figure that rises before wars.
place: Bloody Acre, All Saints Church, Childwall
title: Corpse candles of Bloody Acre, Childwall

desc: A large triangular craft reported over RAF Cosford and RAF Shawbury. Investigated by the MoD's Nick Pope.
title: Cosford incident

desc: An angler photographed a humming metallic disc hovering over the reservoir for more than 15 minutes before it sped off. Checks with the RAF, airports and police found no known traffic.
title: Craigluscar Reservoir metallic disc

desc: An RAF pilot and student flying at 2,000 ft reported an object climbing to around 25,000 ft before appearing to explode. RAF and civil police investigated; no explanation was given.
source: The National Archives – UFO files highlights (March 2009)
title: Cranwell 'possible missile'

desc: Reported ghosts include a lady in white said to be a ballerina, a stagehand, a hooded figure and a lost child; an exorcism was reportedly held in 1969.
place: Lyceum Theatre, Heath Street, Crewe, Cheshire
title: Crewe Lyceum Theatre

desc: In April 2009 a CCTV clip appeared to show a glowing figure moving along a path towards the hall before vanishing, and the council brought in ghost specialists. Earls of Sefton are traditionally said to walk the grounds.
title: Croxteth Hall CCTV figure

desc: A caller told police they had seen an object with eight to ten lights around its edge. No explanation was recorded.
title: Crumlin ringed-light object

desc: Two young princes, legend says, were thrown from the bridge by Roger Mortimer, and their cries are heard on stormy nights.
title: Crying princes at Farndon Bridge

desc: Phantom soldiers and the sounds of battle are said to occur around the 16 April anniversary, and a visitor in 1936 reportedly saw a dead Highlander by a grave mound.
title: Culloden battlefield

desc: A Llandudno couple reported a charcoal-coloured triangular craft over Cwm Mountain, and the following month an egg-shaped object with a sphere suspended beneath it. No explanation was given.
title: Cwm Mountain charcoal triangle

desc: Engineer Mike Dunne, 25, photographed a dark disc-shaped object hovering over houses near Bidston Hill before it vanished; dozens of others were said to have seen it. Slemen calls the hill a UFO 'window area'.
title: Dark disc photographed over Bidston Hill

desc: A local man filmed 40 seconds of daylight video showing a small dark object hovering over the castle. It then sank slowly and disappeared behind the walls.
title: Dark object filmed over Caernarfon Castle

desc: A forestry worker said spiked spheres grabbed him beside a hovering dome. Police recorded it as an assault; ground marks were found.
title: Robert Taylor, Dechmont Woods

desc: Two roe deer carcasses with injuries some experts said matched a big cat kill were sampled by Warwick University. DNA tests found only fox and deer.
title: Deer carcasses at Woodchester Park

desc: Two police constables followed a bright cross-shaped light by car for around 15 minutes and reported a second object joining it. The sighting was attributed to Venus.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Devon 'flying cross' police chase

desc: A Colwyn Bay couple camping at the abbey said a huge, silent diamond-shaped object hovered roughly 60 feet up. They described spotlights that lit the ruins like a stadium and red lights arranged in a cross.
title: Diamond-shaped craft over Valle Crucis Abbey

desc: A fireball was reported travelling across Douglas Bay at night. No explanation was given in the report.
title: Douglas Bay fireball

desc: Visitors report whispers, apparitions, organ music, a phantom carriage and servants' voices in the kitchens.
title: Duckett's Grove

desc: A series of silent black triangle sightings over the Black Country between 2007 and 2011 earned the nickname 'Dudley Dorito'. No explanation was established.
source: Wikipedia – List of reported UFO sightings
title: Dudley 'Dorito' triangles

desc: Lucette, a governess said to have drowned herself after being deceived by an officer, is reported in a winding sheet, especially on Christmas Eve.
title: Dunkenhalgh governess Lucette

desc: Three white objects were reported over the east of the city. Russian Antonov An-30 survey aircraft were put forward as the likely cause.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: East Glasgow three white objects

desc: Residents watched slow-moving lights for about an hour late in the evening. They were attributed to the Northern Lights.
title: East Hull slow lights

desc: A motorcyclist heading for Manchester in the early hours claimed two beings in ski-suit-like outfits stopped and spoke to him. No corroboration was recorded.
title: East Lancs Road roadside aliens

desc: During a 2009 BBC overnight filming, a microphone recorded about 20 minutes of unexplained voices that the presenter did not hear; no source was identified.
title: Edinburgh Vaults voices

desc: During the 1904-05 Welsh revival, preacher Mary Jones and many others reported balls and columns of light around Egryn Chapel and along the Dyffryn-Llanbedr road. Journalists from the Daily Mail, Daily Mirror and Daily News came to investigate, and a local police constable also reported a light he could not explain. Proposed causes include earth lights on the Mochras Fault, marsh gas and gorse fires.
title: Egryn lights and the Mary Jones revival

desc: During a Faenol Festival evening, a Llanfairpwll family and festival-goers watched 11 silent orange lights in small groups travel up the Strait, stop at the Britannia Bridge, turn towards Bangor and climb steeply away. The fireworks had not started yet, and the RAF reported no aircraft.
title: Eleven orange lights over the Menai Strait

desc: Former owner Elizabeth Warburton is seen walking through walls, alongside a Tudor-dressed man, a WWII officer and a grey-haired woman by the piano. Visitors report banging, crying children and footsteps.
title: Elizabeth Warburton of Stanley Palace

desc: West Yorkshire Police logged a possible UFO after officers and other witnesses watched a static cylindrical object with a white light at each end near the TV mast for several minutes. The CAA could not identify it as an aircraft.
title: Emley Moor mast police sighting

desc: Furniture moving, knocking and a gruff voice reported in a council house, investigated by the Society for Psychical Research.
title: Enfield poltergeist

desc: During the NATO Exercise Mainbrace a silver disc was reported following a Meteor jet back towards RAF Topcliffe, and RAF aircraft later chased a sphere over the North Sea. The case was raised in Parliament; no explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Exercise Mainbrace disc over RAF Topcliffe

desc: A police officer reported a large explosion accompanied by an intense white light over the town.
title: Explosion and white light over Rhuddlan

desc: Reported spirits at the former coach house include a Cavalier, a young girl and a Victorian farrier in a leather apron. When a resident told the farrier to leave, he is said to have answered back and vanished. Guests also report drawers opening by themselves.
place: Trevor Arms, Marford Hill, Marford, Wrexham
title: Farrier ghost at the Trevor Arms, Marford

desc: Legend says a man and his son were imprisoned here and the father killed the boy and then himself rather than starve; the pair are said to appear in the room where they died. The castle is now a hotel.
title: Father and son of Leasowe Castle

desc: A large fawn-coloured cat was reported at Strabane, one of several big cat reports from the town since 2004.
title: Fawn-coloured cat at Strabane

desc: A farmer testing a neighbour's big cat sightings caught a female puma in a cage trap. Experts judged her a tame former pet and she lived out her life at the Highland Wildlife Park.
title: Felicity the puma trapped at Cannich

desc: A woman walking three dogs with her partner saw a Labrador-sized brown or black cat with a feline tail, which ran off; she reported it to police. The Fen Tiger has been reported in the area for decades.
title: Fen Tiger seen behind Abbotsley golf club

desc: A local investigator reported five saucer-shaped objects in a row over the sea, then a flash and bang as an RAF aircraft passed. RAF Leeming said he had seen a heat-seeking flare.
title: Filey Brigg five saucers

desc: At 5.15pm a witness saw a shooting-star-like object with a burning tail, about the size of a military jet, apparently falling towards the ground.
title: Fireball in the Ogwen Valley

desc: In the 1960s a bearded phantom fireman in a brass helmet was seen sitting on a ladder; the witness rang the alarm bell and quit soon after.
place: Old Fire Station (Chez Jules), Northgate Street, Chester
title: Fireman Jack of the Old Fire Station

desc: Three men fishing saw a brown or tawny animal about the size of a golden retriever, which they thought was a puma. Another man and his son abandoned a barbecue at the same spot in May after seeing a similar cat.
title: Fishermen meet tawny puma at Gimblet Rock

desc: A man in a flat cap and blue overalls is reported in the Construction Hall and an elderly woman near the kitchen. Staff have also described lights and doors operating by themselves and men in boiler suits vanishing.
title: Flat-capped worker at Cammell Laird

desc: A strangely two-dimensional soldier with sergeant's stripes, a thin moustache and a swagger stick rides trains from Birkenhead Central and steps off at James Street. A lollipop man told Slemen he saw it in the 1990s with other passengers.
title: Flat WWI sergeant on the Birkenhead train

desc: A drowned sailor in blue, said to have been laid out in the inn before burial, floats about the building, sometimes just head and shoulders over a mist; he was also seen 'digging' in the churchyard.
place: Punch Bowl Inn and churchyard, Sefton
title: Floating sailor of the Punch Bowl, Sefton

desc: Four hill walkers said a black animal, possibly a puma, stared at them for a couple of minutes before vanishing into gorse.
title: Four walkers watched by cat on Moel Hiraddug

desc: Four trawler crew reported a flat, shiny round object hovering about 19 miles north-east of Fraserburgh, briefly tracked on the boat's radar before it vanished. No explanation was given.
title: Fraserburgh trawler radar disc

desc: A local reporter counted 16 fast white lights crossing the sky over two nights. RAF Kinloss reported no aircraft; satellites were suggested but considered unusual in that number.
title: Fyvie fast white lights

desc: An elderly woman is said to appear near seat B14 and walk through a wall.
place: Gaiety Theatre, Harris Promenade, Douglas, Isle of Man
title: Gaiety Theatre seat B14

desc: A young woman near the golf course said a black cat bigger than an Alsatian leapt out at her and fled when her dog barked, adding to late-1990s rumours of a Galloway Puma around Kirroughtree.
title: Galloway Puma springs at dog walker

desc: A chapel seat is kept empty for a White Lady thought to be Janet Douglas, and legends tell of a hidden 'monster' and of Earl Beardie gambling with the Devil.
title: Glamis Castle legends

desc: In summer 1983 people saw amber oval lights, then a large H-shaped formation that released smaller lights before folding in on itself and vanishing. Researchers linked it to a wave of sightings over the Clwydian Range, Prestatyn, Meliden and Dyserth in 1985-86.
title: Glan Conwy H-shaped light formation

desc: In 2002 the landlord watched a man walk across the closed bar, glaring at him, then vanish. Later owners report a dark shadow on the back stairs and a lift bell ringing at 2am; Most Haunted visited in 2016.
title: Glaring stranger at the Slaughter House pub

desc: Children playing in the street reported several figures in long white garments floating above the ground. No explanation was offered.
title: Glasgow West End floating figures

desc: A resident reported a silver disc approaching his flat and hovering around 100 ft up, with residents of two neighbouring flats backing his account. No explanation was given.
title: Glasgow Westbourne Gardens disc

desc: Locals saw a bright golden ball of light move very fast, change direction abruptly and disappear. No explanation was given.
title: Glounthaune golden light

desc: A trespasser on the priory ruins said he heard beautiful singing and saw a pair of glowing monks.
title: Glowing monks and singing, Norton Priory

desc: At about 10.30am a resident filmed a triangular object, red on top with a pulsing blue-green light underneath. Over about 20 minutes it hung still, drifted east, then turned west and climbed out of sight. He said he was not claiming it was a UFO.
title: Glowing triangle filmed over Buckley

desc: Drivers have described a golden, futuristic-looking vehicle overtaking at huge speed and disappearing into the tunnel wall, alongside an old 1960s-style police car seen in the early hours. Slemen lists the tunnel as a timeslip spot.
title: Golden car vanishing into Queensway Tunnel wall

desc: A farmer said he fired at a large golden cat on his land.
title: Golden 'leopard cat' shot at, Crewood Hall Farm

desc: The pub is said to be haunted by Jeffrey, a ploughman hanged for murder and gibbeted nearby, who is blamed for moving bottles and overturning glasses and chairs, especially in bedroom two.
place: The Golden Lion, Chester Road, Rossett, Wrexham
title: Golden Lion ploughman, Rossett

desc: Locals told of a giant figure glittering in gold seen on the burial mound for years before workmen dug up the Bronze Age Mold gold cape there in 1833. A former servant said she saw it 14 years earlier. The ghost is said not to have been seen since.
title: Golden spectre of Bryn yr Ellyllon, Mold

desc: During a 2018 ghost hunt at Ruthin's timber-framed town house, guests reported nausea, fainting and burning eyes. A doll used as a trigger object fell from its chair and moved out of a chalk circle. The doll is now kept at Tatton Old Hall.
place: Nantclwyd y Dre, Castle Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
title: Grace the doll at Nantclwyd y Dre

desc: At 2.30am one summer night at least four army cadets saw a legless green lady in an old-fashioned dress float across the fields towards the church.
place: Fields by St Helen's Church, Sefton
title: Green lady seen by cadets, Sefton

desc: On New Year's Eve a dark grey, Labrador-sized cat was reported beside the A548 where the national speed limit begins. An earlier report came from near Mostyn on New Year's Day 2015.
title: Grey cat on A548 at Tanlan, Talacre

desc: A motionless orange light was reported growing to several times its size, turning red and blue, then moving west. No explanation was given.
title: Greystones growing orange light

desc: A walker on the path at about 3.45am heard a loud growl from a sheltered spot and saw a brown or tawny big cat. She switched off her head torch and kept silent.
title: Growl from the dark on Snowdon's Pyg Track

desc: A floating woman in white, said to be the Countess of Dundonald, is reported mostly in her tower. A 2010 photo reportedly shows a pale figure at a banqueting-hall window where there was no floor to stand on. Staff describe footsteps and gate chains rattling at night.
title: Gwrych Castle countess and window figure

desc: A floating woman in white, linked to the Countess of Dundonald, has been reported since the 1950s, mostly around the Countess's Tower. In 2010 a prospective buyer photographed a pale figure at a banqueting hall window where the floor had rotted away.
title: Gwrych Castle White Woman

desc: In 1995 workmen found an old dog skeleton under the cellar floor, and a phantom dog has been reported since. A grey lady, preceded by a smell of decay, is linked to a maid said to have been walled up in the north wing.
title: Gwydir Castle ghost dog and grey lady

desc: Writer T Gwynn Jones recorded in 1930 that his grandmother's horse shied as a huge mastiff-like dog passed on the road home from Ruthin, unseen by her husband. A former yeomanry sergeant also described a Gwyllgi trailing him over the moors from Cynwyd fair in the 1920s.
title: Gwyllgi hound near Ruthin

desc: Visitors and staff describe a young woman's apparition, an aggressive male presence and a man in period uniform.
place: Hack Green Secret Nuclear Bunker, near Nantwich, Cheshire
title: Hack Green Nuclear Bunker

desc: A witness described a seven-foot figure with short dark hair and glowing red eyes for about eight seconds at the hillfort. A 1995 motorist on the Cannock-Rugeley road reported a similar hairy man-like figure.
title: Hairy giant at Castle Ring, Cannock Chase

desc: Reported ghosts include a lady in grey called Sarah, her brother Albert, a figure by the organ, and a former employee who took his own life.
title: Hand Hotel Chirk grey lady

desc: A girl named Harriet, said to have died falling on the stairs in 1861, is reported screaming, laughing and singing at night.
title: Harriet of Charleville Castle

desc: Two teenage joggers heard hooves behind them and turned to see a headless horse's body draped in something like a tablecloth, which had gone when they looked again.
title: Headless horse on Springwood Avenue

desc: A Royalist soldier decapitated by a cannon ball while lodging here is said to haunt the house, along with a grey lady.
place: Tudor House, Lower Bridge Street, Chester
title: Headless Royalist of Tudor House

desc: A servant beheaded by Cromwell's men for hiding her master's treasure walks the old path; she appeared so often that the nearby inn took the name Headless Woman.
place: Bridle path from Hockenhull Hall, near Tarvin
title: Headless woman of Hockenhull

desc: A figure in a headmaster's gown, called Mr McGraw, was seen and heard; one cleaner persuaded the caretaker to arm himself with a pistol and search.
title: Headmaster's ghost at Oldershaw, Wallasey

desc: Two air traffic controllers reported a black inverted-boomerang-shaped object seen from the control tower in the morning. No explanation is recorded in the released file.
source: The National Archives – UFO files highlights (March 2009)
title: Heathrow controllers' boomerang

desc: A driver crossing the Chase reported a falling light followed by a huge black dog; a couple later described a misty figure crossing Coal Pit Lane, Brereton, in 1985.
title: Hellhound of Brereton

desc: Two Horsham police officers reported lights in the sky and a beam shining down to the ground. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Henfield police lights and beam

desc: Henrietta killed herself in the cellar after learning her Royalist lover died at Rowton Moor; her figure climbs to an upstairs window to wait for him.
place: Blue Bell Inn, Northgate Street, Chester
title: Henrietta at the Blue Bell window

desc: Three witnesses watched a cigar-shaped object with two red lights travel silently over the area at a slow, airship-like pace. No explanation was given.
title: Hessle Road silent cigar

desc: A wolf blamed for livestock deaths roamed the Hexham area in the winter of 1904. It was later linked to the wolf-man figures reported in connection with the Hexham Heads in the 1970s.
title: Hexham wolf livestock killings

desc: Two police officers on duty reported a large white object in the sky. No explanation was recorded.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Hindley police sighting

desc: Staff keep a file of incidents; the most frequent is a Green Lady in velvet, with a little girl, a monk and a black dog also reported.
place: Hoghton Tower, Hoghton, near Preston, Lancashire
title: Hoghton Tower Green Lady

desc: A round, bright white object hovered and then moved slowly and quietly from south-west to north-east in the afternoon. No explanation was given.
title: Holyhead hovering white object

desc: A bright star-like light pulsing red and green hung stationary in the morning before moving away. MoD files record no explanation.
title: Holyhead pulsating light

desc: Two robed and hooded monks are said to drift along the walls, turrets and quayside and are seen as omens of disaster. Dogs reportedly refuse to pass the castle gate.
title: Hooded monks of Conwy Castle

desc: Two sonic booms were recorded and a large search for a crashed aircraft found nothing, with a triangular UFO reported an hour earlier. The RAF denied any supersonic flights.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Howden Moor booms and triangle

desc: On 24 March 1997 police, gamekeepers and farmers reported a low, lit aircraft and an explosion; a search across 40 square miles found no wreckage.
place: Howden Reservoir and moors, Upper Derwent, South Yorkshire/Derbyshire
title: Howden Moor phantom aircraft

desc: Hugh Gray's blurred image near Foyers was the first claimed photograph of the monster. Analysts have suggested it shows his Labrador swimming with a stick, or an otter.
title: Hugh Gray's first Nessie photograph

desc: A silver dome-shaped object was seen near the bridge appearing to change from cigar to circular shape, hover, then move off. No explanation was given.
place: Humber Bridge, East Riding of Yorkshire
title: Humber Bridge shape-shifting dome

desc: Witnesses from Cleethorpes, Grimsby, Hull and Flamborough described a slow, silent triangular or diamond-shaped object at a few hundred feet with no contrail. No explanation was found.
title: Humber coast silent triangle

desc: Witnesses described a triangular craft up to 200 ft across, covered in lights and making a noise like a lawnmower, before it vanished.
title: Humming triangle over Bangor

desc: A Glasgow family saw something large with humps swimming about 200 yards off the east shore and reported it to police in Dumbarton.
title: Humped creature in Loch Lomond reported to police

desc: William Huskisson MP, killed by Stephenson's Rocket in 1830, is said to limp from his mausoleum in the sunken cemetery below the Anglican Cathedral. The chalybeate spring there is linked in lore to a witch called Jenna Green.
place: St James's Cemetery, Hope Street, Liverpool
title: Huskisson's limping ghost, St James's Cemetery

desc: A walker said he photographed a small green figure and lost time. Near the Twelve Apostles stones.
title: Ilkley Moor alien photograph

desc: A caretaker named Les is said to have fallen on the icy roof and died of exposure, and staff blame him for unexplained noises and figures in photos. A red-cardiganed old lady and a Cavalier have also been reported.
place: Royal Court Theatre, Roe Street, Liverpool
title: 'It must have been Les' at the Royal Court

desc: Two young joggers saw a car-sized object with coloured lights around its rim and a red light underneath hovering over the pass. It sped off over the mountain within about ten seconds, and they reported it to police.
title: Joggers see lit craft over Sychnant Pass

desc: Beatles fans have reported a white-suited Lennon looking out of the bedroom window of his childhood home after it was restored by the National Trust. One fan claimed a night-vision camera caught a figure at the window.
title: John Lennon at the Mendips window

desc: Investigator Russ Kellett said a bright light hovered over him while he waited on his motorbike, leaving red marks on his hands, neck and face. No explanation was given.
place: Level crossing near Keighley, West Yorkshire
title: Keighley level crossing burns

desc: A BBC Tomorrow's World team caught a live female of the large black 'Kellas cat' after a gamekeeper had snared one in 1984. Museum study showed the animals are wildcat-domestic cat hybrids.
title: Kellas cat caught on the Kellas estate

desc: Strange lights and shapes were reported above the town for several hours, including a large triangular craft trailing multicoloured light. No explanation was given.
title: Kells lights and triangle

desc: Three naval cadets walked into a village that looked medieval, silent and empty, then found it normal when they returned.
title: Kersey time slip

desc: A family driving through Holderness saw three lights flying in a spearhead formation, one in front and two behind. No explanation was given.
title: Keyingham spearhead lights

desc: Unseen presences are said to switch the chapel lights on and off and slam cell doors.
title: Kilmainham Gaol

desc: A man reported a 200 ft blue triangle hovering over his garden at 4am before shooting away, leaving a white substance on trees that he collected. The MoD file gives no explanation.
title: Kingstanding blue triangle residue

desc: A wailing woman in white with dark eye sockets is said to roam the grounds around 4am, and two driverless vintage cars with glaring headlamps haunt the estate roads. A Welsh paranormal group photographed an 'orb' there in 2009.
title: Knowsley Hall banshee and phantom cars

desc: A couple driving uphill saw a big black cat about the size of a Labrador, with a long black tail, cross in front of their car. They reported it to Puma Watch North Wales.
title: Labrador-sized black cat crosses road, Colwyn Heights

desc: Marford's cottages have cross-shaped windows said to ward off evil. The village's best-known ghost is Lady Margaret Blackbourne, said to have been murdered by her husband in 1713.
title: Lady Blackbird of Marford

desc: Guests and staff report a wild-looking woman with an axe in the corridors, banqueting hall and battlements, said to be a medieval lady who killed her husband's lover. A one-gloved soldier and a giggling girl who knocks on doors are also described.
title: Lady Grey of Ruthin Castle

desc: Visitors to the Tudor manor report footsteps, a baby crying and a shadowy figure. The haunting is linked to a legend that a lady of the house killed her infant and then herself after her husband's gambling losses.
title: Lady Mary of Speke Hall

desc: In October 1982 a couple in a layby saw a Lancaster-type bomber over the moonlit reservoir vanish before their eyes; another couple later reported a silent four-engined bomber by the viaduct.
title: Ladybower phantom Lancaster

desc: USAF and RAF radar operators tracked a number of fast-moving targets and an RAF Venom pilot sent to intercept reported a luminous object on radar and visually. It remains officially unexplained.
source: Wikipedia – List of reported UFO sightings
title: Lakenheath–Bentwaters radar-visual case

desc: A caller told North Wales Police that a dead lamb left in a barn overnight had been stripped to the bone, and linked it to a big cat. Police looked into it but the outcome was not recorded.
title: Lamb carcass stripped in barn, Ruthin

desc: The castle, site of the 1612 witch trials and later a prison, has reports of shadowy figures, cold spots and crying.
title: Lancaster Castle

desc: Slemen counts over forty ghosts on Rodney Street, including a caped, top-hatted figure called Lantern Jaw and a shorter man linked to William Mackenzie's pyramid tomb in St Andrew's churchyard, who are seen to argue. Phantom carriages are also heard.
title: Lantern Jaw and the pyramid ghost, Rodney Street

desc: Rural police received a report of a larger-than-usual cat crossing the A5 between Chirk and Llangollen in the early hours, and asked the public not to approach any such animal.
title: Large cat crossing A5 near Chirk

desc: At about 2.30am a silent object bigger than a helicopter, with a bar-like part, was seen roughly 250 m up. After about half a minute it headed out over the sea with a helicopter close behind.
title: Large object followed by helicopter, Old Colwyn

desc: Known for its Bloody Chapel and an 'elemental' publicised by Mildred Darby, the castle also reports a dagger-carrying Red Lady and two girls.
place: Leap Castle, near Roscrea, Co Offaly
title: Leap Castle Red Lady

desc: Three people in a car reported being lit by a coloured beam for more than two minutes. No explanation was given.
place: Glen Road, near Lennoxtown, East Dunbartonshire
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Lennoxtown coloured beam

desc: A Leeds University student and friends saw a very muscular cat with leopard-like markings on a rock about 20 metres away; another group of men also saw it. He photographed the animal.
place: Cow and Calf rocks, Ilkley Moor, West Yorkshire
title: Leopard-marked cat at the Cow and Calf

desc: Walking home at about 2am on 2 January 1950, Miss E.F. Smith reported torch-bearing figures searching for bodies in fields, later linked to the 685 battle of Nechtanesmere.
place: near Letham, below Dunnichen Hill, Angus
title: Letham phantom battle

desc: A lioness was reported roaming the Upton area of Chester; police searched but found nothing.
title: Lioness reported at Upton

desc: A girl is said to appear on the second floor, where a nursery once was. Guests report hearing her tricycle at night and having their hair tugged while running baths.
place: The Queen Hotel, City Road, Chester, Cheshire
title: Little girl on the Queen Hotel's second floor

desc: A family driving at night said a purple triangular craft engulfed their car and they lost several hours. The driver later said a small black object fell from his mouth, and that air force personnel told the family to keep quiet.
title: Little Orme purple triangle and missing time

desc: A tearful Victorian girl has been seen in the bars, and a dark apparition in a dressing room reportedly stopped once the room became a store.
place: Liverpool Empire Theatre, Lime Street, Liverpool
title: Liverpool Empire Theatre girl

desc: The Tudor manor was listed among the UK's top haunted places in 2007; a Wales Online journalist spent a night there in 2018 and described four spirits it is said to host.
title: Llancaiach Fawr Manor

desc: A couple described an egg-shaped object gliding and jumping above their home before turning spherical and speeding into cloud; weeks later they reported a ball of light over the Orme cliffs. No explanation was given.
title: Llandudno Easter-egg object

desc: A farmer out shooting saw a bright white light come down slowly. Soon afterwards a mother at her window saw three tall figures in silver-grey suits walking across a field as cows stampeded. A catalogue review rates the case weak and suggests firefighters in protective suits.
title: Llanerchymedd silver figures in a field

desc: Concert-goers reported a disc-shaped object in blue, green, white and orange moving slowly up and down. MoD files record no explanation.
title: Llanfyllin four-colour disc

desc: The wife of a retired Royal Marine said a light came into her bedroom, its surface pulsing as if with energy, and later left through the window.
title: Llangefni bedroom ball of light

desc: A local shop manager filmed pulsing, colour-changing spheres over his property over several weeks, once counting 13 in a night. Police passed it to the MoD, which gave no explanation.
title: Llannefydd colour-changing spheres

desc: A fireball or meteorite was reported plunging into the reservoir, according to MoD files. No confirmed explanation was recorded.
title: Llyn Cefni fireball

desc: Legend says Anne Tottenham saw a cloven foot on a card-playing stranger who vanished through the roof; she declined and died in 1775 and is said to haunt the house.
place: Loftus Hall, Hook Peninsula, Co Wexford
title: Loftus Hall card game

desc: At 2.35am a resident watched a large black cat with a tail several feet long cross a paddock about 100 yards away for a couple of minutes. Horses in the paddock seemed undisturbed.
title: Long-tailed black cat at Treuddyn

desc: A worker arriving at dawn saw a large, slender cat-like animal with a very long tail. Later that morning he photographed a possible paw print in mud about 300 metres away.
title: Long-tailed cat and paw print, Ince Marshes

desc: Long tradition of lights on Bleaklow and the Devil's Elbow, alongside ghostly aircraft stories from the many crash sites.
title: Longdendale lights

desc: Children reported a silver egg-shaped object landing in the park and lifting off silently as they ran towards it. A small helicopter was suggested but never confirmed.
title: Longhill Park egg-shaped landing

desc: College students filming a class project posted a clip of a dark object moving on the surface and diving. Critics suggested a marine animal and questioned whether the footage was staged.
title: Lough Foyle 'monster' video

desc: Three priests fishing on the lough watched an animal roughly six feet long with a head about 18 inches across from about 100 yards away. The story was carried locally and later by the BBC.
title: Lough Ree monster seen by three priests

desc: Numerous witnesses reported a large triangular craft with three lights that hovered, rotated and shot upwards at speed. The MoD file gives no explanation.
source: The National Archives – UFO files highlights (March 2009)
title: Louth triangle seen by many

desc: Two lynx believed to have been illegally released were caught in bait traps and taken to the Highland Wildlife Park; two more were seen in the area the next day.
title: Lynx captured at Drumguish

desc: A witness reported an animal resembling a lynx at the roadside on Mold Road near Wrexham. Police investigated without finding it.
title: Lynx-like animal on Mold Road, Gwersyllt

desc: A dog walker thought he saw a lynx on the golf course, and three more people later came forward with similar accounts.
title: Lynx of the links, Eyemouth

desc: A bright oblong object with a rounded end was reported hovering silently over the coast. No explanation was given.
title: Mablethorpe hovering oblong

desc: A couple driving the new A82 saw a whale-bodied animal rolling in the loch. Its report in the Inverness Courier popularised the word 'monster' and began the modern Nessie story.
title: Mackays see whale-like creature, Loch Ness

desc: Visitors near Sir George Mackenzie's Black Mausoleum report scratches, burns and fainting, and the area is generally locked except for tours.
title: Mackenzie Poltergeist, Greyfriars

desc: In 1982 a guest in room 6 watched a silent man in black for about 15 minutes. Other reports include a child spirit, writing appearing on the room 4 mirror, and items vanishing. A sword found under a room 4 floorboard hangs on the wall.
place: Ye Olde King's Head, Lower Bridge Street, Chester, Cheshire
title: Man in black in room 6, Ye Olde King's Head

desc: The pub stands on the line of the Roman road out of the fortress, and landlords and drinkers have reported marching feet in the cellars following the old route. The pub closed in 2023.
place: George and Dragon, Liverpool Road, Chester
title: Marching legion under the George and Dragon

desc: In November 1932 two friends driving across the battlefield saw three men in Cavalier-style cloaks and hats who vanished as the car slowed; a group of tourists reported similar 17th-century figures in 1968.
place: Marston Moor, Long Marston, North Yorkshire
title: Marston Moor Cavaliers

desc: The buried 17th-century close has a long haunting reputation and has been investigated repeatedly; one suggestion is that marsh gas from the Nor Loch caused eerie lights.
place: Mary King's Close, Royal Mile, Edinburgh
title: Mary King's Close

desc: A man out running saw a huge black animal he took to be a melanistic leopard; the same day a dog walker at nearby Bryn Cadno reported a fast-moving puma.
title: Melanistic leopard seen by runner, Llysfaen

desc: A man at a bus stop reported a railway-carriage-shaped object with three windows and swirling yellow smoke passing about 20 ft overhead, and a sense that time had stood still. No explanation was given.
title: Menock Road floating carriage

desc: An eastbound triangular object was reported sweeping silently overhead in the evening. No explanation was given.
title: Middlesbrough silent triangle

desc: A witness watched a silent midnight funeral pass, complete with coffin and deathly pale mourners, and later learned a secret funeral had once set out from a nearby hall.
title: Midnight phantom funeral, Knotty Ash

desc: Lee Jones, his wife and her mother watched a vast saucer hover, partly hidden by cloud; a passing airliner let him estimate it at a mile across. Others reported it earlier that year.
title: Mile-long saucer over Anfield

desc: Called the island's most haunted house, it is said to host a former lady of the house and a hostile spirit.
place: Milntown, near Ramsey, Isle of Man
title: Milntown, Ramsey

desc: A phantom black dog is said to haunt the castle; in Waldron's 1731 account a drunken guard who went alone through its passage returned speechless and died days later.
place: Peel Castle, St Patrick's Isle, Peel, Isle of Man
title: Moddey Dhoo of Peel Castle

desc: National Archives papers record a UFO over Moelfre described as looking like a Chinese lantern, which is the likely explanation.
title: Moelfre lantern-like UFO

desc: Angus Brooks reported watching a translucent craft with movable girder-like arms hover for about 22 minutes on the downs. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Moigns Down 'girder' craft

desc: A landlady saw a monk kneeling in prayer in the tower room in 1980, just after a family accident. In 1991 a barman said a very tall figure with a small boy lunged at him. The monk is said to warn of bad news.
place: Liverpool Arms, Lower Gate Street, Conwy
title: Monk and lunging figure at the Liverpool Arms

desc: Reports of a serpent-like animal date from 1887, with 34 incidents counted by 1981. In the best-known case two local men said their boat struck a 25-30 ft humped creature, which they fended off with an oar and a rifle shot.
title: Morag of Loch Morar

desc: Scientists surveying fish with sonar recorded a large solid object, prompting talk of a lake monster nicknamed Muckie. Seals surfacing in pairs have been suggested as an explanation for sightings.
title: Muckie sonar contact, Lakes of Killarney

desc: A misty outline of a man, said to be a miller murdered in the early 1800s, has been reported many times around the windmill on Bidston Hill. Local lore also ties the hill to covens and a buried occultist named Richard Tilly.
title: Murdered miller at Bidston Windmill

desc: A resident reported a bright, stationary light high on the ridge above the Tal-y-llyn pass, and 16 rescue volunteers went out. Through binoculars they found that trees on the ridge had been hung with solar fairy lights.
title: Mystery light on Cadair Idris ridge

desc: Since the 15th-century timbered town house opened as a museum in 2007, staff and visitors have reported a lady in white and poltergeist activity. Investigators also linked a spirit to a doll known as Grace.
place: Nantclwyd y Dre, Castle Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
title: Nantclwyd y Dre White Lady

desc: Residents reported a mid-air explosion, prompting a search by an RAF Nimrod and helicopters. Nothing was found and no explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Ness mid-air explosion

desc: A wartime radar guard, Albert Lancaster, later claimed he had been caught in a beam and felt himself floating while on duty near the coast. No explanation is recorded.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Newbiggin radar guard beam claim

desc: The former orphanage and hospital has reports of a nurse's apparition, child ghosts and banging from old punishment cupboards.
place: Newsham Park Hospital, Newsham Park, Liverpool
title: Newsham Park Hospital

desc: A black triangular object with green lights was reported over the town. No explanation was given.
title: Northallerton black triangle

desc: Artist Reginald Easton woke to an old woman by his bed and stayed a week to sketch her; she is said to have murdered a child at the hall.
title: Old woman drawn by Reginald Easton, Thurstaston

desc: A night-shift crew at a dockside mill watched a fuzzy orange ball hang over Liverpool Bay, dart across to hover over the Dee, then shoot upwards and vanish. The witness recalls the Liverpool Echo reporting many calls from along the coast.
title: Orange ball over Mersey and Dee from Wallasey Docks

desc: In summer 1974 two women leaving the old psychiatric hospital saw a round, bright orange light that shot away at great speed. Similar lights were reported over the Denbigh Moors in 1984 and 1994.
title: Orange light over Denbigh Hospital

desc: On New Year's Eve a father and son watched a bright orange light, which they judged much brighter than the ISS, vanish and reappear on a steady track for two to three minutes. The RAF referred them to a UFO hotline the MoD had just closed.
title: Orange light seen from Mynydd Mechell

desc: Over several weeks a Benllech resident saw fuzzy, non-pulsing orange lights rise over the sea from the direction of Beaumaris and Puffin Island. On 8 August three moved together, and a fourth crossed her view, shrank and vanished.
title: Orange lights from Puffin Island direction

desc: Drinkers at the Piccadilly Inn and the Royal Oak went outside to watch bright orange circular lights crossing the sky one Wednesday evening. One self-described sceptic said he could not explain what he saw.
title: Orange lights over Caerwys pubs

desc: A retired post office engineer from Llandudno was walking in a gale when he saw an oval object, white on top and dark underneath. It stopped, moved on, and disappeared into a glow.
title: Oval object on Conwy Mountain

desc: Children reported a large owl-like man-creature above the church tower.
title: Owlman of Mawnan

desc: Around 6am a dog walker saw a black panther-like cat chasing rabbits and birds before it ran fast across the beach.
title: Panther hunting on Ffrith Beach

desc: Walkers descending Pen-y-ghent photographed a trail of large, fresh prints in snow. A British Big Cats Society researcher judged from the photos that they could be from a puma or lynx.
title: Paw prints in snow on Pen-y-ghent

desc: Ghosts of the 1612 Pendle witches are said to roam the hill, and during a live Most Haunted broadcast on Halloween 2004 team members at a nearby farmhouse reported choking sensations.
title: Pendle Hill witches

desc: Witnesses described a pyramid of light descending and releasing objects, followed by military aircraft and explosions. The MoD said it was a routine exercise but withheld some details.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Pentyrch pyramid of light

desc: From 1979 staff at a mower shop reported thrown stones, moving tools and appearing coins; SPR investigator David Fontana studied it from 1989 to 1992.
place: Mower Services, Crwys Road, Cathays, Cardiff
title: Pete the Cardiff Poltergeist

desc: A photograph of two humps near Urquhart Castle was later attributed to wakes from trawlers, and differences between negative and print raised suspicion of doctoring.
title: Peter MacNab's humps photo, Urquhart Castle

desc: Shepherds and villagers reported spectral armies re-fighting the battle around Christmas 1642, described in a January 1643 pamphlet; a royal commission was said to have witnessed it.
title: Phantom battle of Edgehill

desc: In January 1816 the Keeper of the Crown Jewels described a floating apparition, and a sentry who met a bear-like shape reportedly died two days later.
place: Martin Tower, Tower of London, London
title: Phantom bear of the Martin Tower

desc: A white city briefly appeared above Liverpool; it was put down to a mirage of Edinburgh, although nobody could pick out any of its buildings.
title: Phantom city in the sky over Liverpool

desc: A married couple told the Daily Post they believe they saw a monk-like ghost on the outskirts of Holywell.
title: Phantom monk outside Holywell

desc: A pillion passenger killed in a 1960s motorbike crash is said to appear in the tunnel and make drivers swerve. A vintage police car has also reportedly been seen.
title: Phantom rider in the Queensway Tunnel

desc: Witnesses on the Abergele coast have described a large ship crewed by Viking-like men that vanished moments after it was seen. It is linked to the legend of Prince Madoc's lost voyage.
title: Phantom ship off Abergele

desc: The cellar of this old coaching inn is said to be haunted by a man who died after falling down its stairs in 1609. Two bedrooms are linked to ghostly chambermaids.
place: The Pied Bull, 57 Northgate Street, Chester, Cheshire
title: Pied Bull cellar and chambermaids

desc: The headless ghost of Piers Gaveston, beheaded in 1312, is said to appear by the barbican and on the battlements and to lure people towards the cliff edge.
title: Piers Gaveston, Scarborough Castle

desc: A volunteer saw a black dog on a landing, a small child said an angry man was in a servants' bed, and a custodian keeps smelling pipe tobacco in the gatehouse shop. A local writer reported a girl in blue and a Civil War figure in the courtyard.
title: Plas Mawr black dog and pipe smoke

desc: Jacobean house near Mold often called the most haunted house in Wales. Reports of a woman in the grounds and apparitions inside.
title: Plas Teg haunting

desc: The house is reputedly haunted by a Victorian daughter of the owners who left to marry a tinker and was later abandoned.
place: Plas yn Rhiw, Rhiw, Llŷn, Gwynedd
title: Plas yn Rhiw Victorian girl

desc: Village claimed to have a dozen or more resident ghosts, including a highwayman and a screaming man.
title: Pluckley

desc: A mother and her teenage daughter driving through the holiday park at about 2am saw a large pointy-eared animal, too big for a fox, run in front of the car into hedges.
place: Hafan y Mor holiday park, Pwllheli, Gwynedd
title: Pointy-eared cat runs past car, Hafan y Mor

desc: An officer was sent after a member of the public reported a strange light at 9.10pm. A police inspector confirmed that officers also saw a light that grew and shrank before fading away.
title: Police officers see light over Penmaenmawr

desc: Visitors to the former manor describe an aggressive presence. Reports include stones being thrown, bruising to the face, unexplained noises and shadowy figures.
title: Pool Parc stone-throwing spirit

desc: Investigators describe an aggressive presence at the former hospital, which closed in 1989, with reports of thrown stones, unexplained bruising, noises and shadowy figures.
place: Pool Park, Efenechtyd, near Ruthin, Denbighshire
title: Pool Park former hospital

desc: After four sheep were killed, police marksmen and RSPCA officials cornered a cat in a barn, but it escaped through a rear exit.
title: Powys Puma escapes police marksmen, Llangurig

desc: Two friends heard a loud aircraft-like noise and saw a green saucer-shaped object for a few seconds before it rose into cloud, and took photos. No explanation was given.
title: Prescot green saucer

desc: An air traffic controller tracked a fast-moving unidentified target on radar. An RAF investigation found nothing to corroborate it.
title: Prestwick radar target

desc: A resident who had seen pumas in the Pyrenees said one stood by his shed facing him for about five seconds before running off. He called police within ten minutes.
title: Puma in an Abersoch back garden

desc: A local man walking his dog watched a very large cat in long grass below St Mary's House for several minutes and later identified it as a puma from pictures.
title: Puma in the Meadows, Overton-on-Dee

desc: A motorist nearly hit a jet-black, Labrador-high cat with a thick curled tail on the A96 by Huntly Industrial Estate.
title: Puma-like cat on A96, Huntly

desc: A villager saw a dog-sized black cat-shaped animal sprint across a field, and a walker filmed a large black cat crossing a lane nearby. Repeated reports led a Senedd member to call for a government investigation.
title: Puma of Pontybodkin

desc: A driver stopping in a lay-by watched a puma-sized cat standing on its hind legs clawing at a litter bin before it slipped into undergrowth. He and his wife had seen a similar cat on the same road that July.
title: Puma raiding litter bin, Fochabers

desc: A puma was reported at Limavady in December 2004, following reports of large black cats there that June.
title: Puma reported at Limavady

desc: Four pupils and their teacher on a school trip saw a long snake-like shape drop into the loch; the teacher compared it to a big python.
title: Python-like creature at Loch Morlich

desc: An RAF flight lieutenant and two colleagues watched two luminous objects over the sea about three miles offshore for well over an hour, while base radar held them in the same position. The MoD report was released years later without an explanation.
title: RAF Boulmer radar-tracked objects

desc: An unidentified object was reported buzzing the control tower. The MoD found no record in air traffic logs and suggested a routine low-flying training sortie.
title: RAF Valley control tower 'buzzing'

desc: Robert Bennett told the St Helens Star he chased a strange craft across the sky with police and radio hams; three officers watched it lift off after landing in a field.
title: Rainhill landing chased by police

desc: Several residents saw and filmed two linked red lights moving slowly and silently over Wrexham, and similar lights were reported near Sandycroft. A reader later identified them as two Royal Navy Lynx helicopters on night-flying training.
title: Red lights over Gwersyllt were helicopters

desc: USAF personnel from RAF Woodbridge reported lights and a craft in the forest over several nights. Deputy base commander Charles Halt recorded a memo and audio tape.
title: Rendlesham Forest incident

desc: Nine schoolgirl netball players reported a strange object over the village and later drew what they saw, days after the Broad Haven school case. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Rhosybol netball team sighting

desc: A large black object was reported over the town. No explanation was given.
title: Rhyl large black object

desc: Robert Rines's expedition recorded sonar targets and an underwater 'rhomboid flipper' image. Rines later accepted the image may have been retouched.
title: Rines 'flipper' photograph, Urquhart Bay

desc: A figure in 19th-century dress, said to be Lady Alicia Ingilby, walks towards the children's rooms through a locked door; Civil War soldiers shot after Marston Moor are also reported.
title: Ripley Castle mourning mother

desc: A driver crossing Belmont reported two rotating circles of light, one inside the other, turning in opposite directions above Rivington. A similar sight had been reported over Winter Hill weeks earlier.
title: Rivington Pike counter-rotating rings

desc: A Roman soldier is said to patrol the walls between Newgate and the amphitheatre. Legend says he was murdered after leaving his post to visit a local girl.
place: City Walls near Newgate, Chester, Cheshire
title: Roman sentry on Chester's walls

desc: In 1953 apprentice plumber Harry Martindale, working in the cellar, saw a column of Roman soldiers and a horse emerge from the wall, visible only from the knees up. He repeated the account unchanged for decades.
title: Roman soldiers, Treasurer's House

desc: A bus driver saw a shiny black cat about the height of a Rottweiler with a curled tail rise from a field, stare at the bus and run off.
title: Rottweiler-sized black cat, Rockcliffe

desc: The 1645 Civil War battlefield is said to be visited by a fallen Royalist commander around the 24 September anniversary. Music by Charles I's court composer William Lawes, who died there, is reportedly heard across the moor.
title: Rowton Moor battle ghost and phantom music

desc: The hotel's former landlord David Pritchard is said to walk its corridors.
title: Royal Goat Hotel landlord, Beddgelert

desc: Reported presences include a cloaked lady, a nun and a shadow in the bar, with staff describing TVs switching themselves on and whispered questions in corridors.
place: Royal Oak Hotel, Holyhead Road, Betws-y-Coed, Conwy
title: Royal Oak Hotel, Betws-y-Coed

desc: In August 2016 a family reported clothes thrown, lights switching and lampshades inverted, with police witnessing events.
title: Rutherglen Poltergeist

desc: The former prison is said to be haunted by William Hughes, the only man hanged there, in 1903, for murdering his wife. Visitors report voices, slamming cell doors and being touched, and a vanished guard is also said to linger.
place: Ruthin Gaol, Clwyd Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
title: Ruthin Gaol hanged prisoner

desc: Visitors report voices, being touched or pushed, and heavy cell doors slamming by themselves. The spirits are linked to William Hughes, the only man hanged there in 1903, a former guard and a young girl.
place: Ruthin Gaol, Clwyd Street, Ruthin, Denbighshire
title: Ruthin Gaol slamming doors

desc: A 17-year-old pupil heard a noise and saw a bright, fuzzy white object with flashing lights move then speed away. A local astronomer suggested a satellite, Venus or a meteor.
title: Rydal School fuzzy light

desc: Two guardsmen saw a white form on the roof in 1957, and in 1973 a Yeoman Warder reported a glow and a touch on his neck; dogs are said to avoid the tower.
place: Salt Tower, Tower of London, London
title: Salt Tower presences

desc: Dorothy Southworth, said to have died of a broken heart, is the hall's White Lady, and motorists on the nearby road have reported seeing her.
place: Samlesbury Hall, Preston New Road, Samlesbury, Lancashire
title: Samlesbury Hall White Lady

desc: A spirit known as Sarah, said to be a jilted bride who hanged herself, is blamed for moving objects and pushing people on the stairs of this old shop. In 1991 heart-shaped chocolate boxes were reportedly found scattered across the floor.
title: Sarah the poltergeist of Eastgate Street

desc: From 22 November 1960, knocks and moving objects centred on 11-year-old Virginia Campbell were witnessed by doctors, a minister and her teacher, at home and in class.
title: Sauchie Poltergeist
