desc: A woman on a flat balcony watched a floating light change shape, brighten, hover and drift out of sight. She rejected a Chinese lantern because of the shape change.
title: Scholes shape-changing light

desc: Children playing on the disused tracks were chased by a pale, witch-like figure that glided without moving its legs; one said her mouth opened impossibly wide. Lore names her as a jilted witch killed by a train.
title: Screeching Ginny at Garston Dock station

desc: Between 10 and 16 very bright lights were reported travelling north at speed in an arrow formation. No explanation was given.
title: Scunthorpe arrow of lights

desc: Around 1990-91 two friends walking home late saw a man-shaped black shadow seven or eight feet tall. Both felt a menacing presence and ran.
title: Seven-foot black shadow in Flint

desc: A British Airways pilot told Shannon air traffic control an object had passed her aircraft at very high speed off the west coast, and other pilots reported similar lights. The Irish Aviation Authority investigated and a meteor or re-entering debris was suggested.
title: Shannon pilots' high-speed lights

desc: A walker watched a pale grey form rise from the canal, change shape and wrap him in a clammy mist before he broke free and ran.
place: Canal towpath by Griffiths' Steam Mill, Chester
title: Shape-shifting figure from the canal, Chester

desc: A sheep was found with its flesh stripped away and North Yorkshire Police's rural crime officer said the evidence fitted a possible big cat attack. Another carcass had been found days earlier at nearby Whashton.
source: Mysterious Britain & Ireland (citing The York Press)
title: Sheep stripped to skeleton, Ravensworth

desc: A cluster of black 'panther' sightings around Shotts in early 2011 drew attention before quickly dying away.
title: Shotts panther flap

desc: A shaggy black creature with a dog's body and a monkey's face was said to haunt the lane between West Wratting and Balsham; the stories were published in 1954 and no sightings are known after the Second World War.
place: Slough Hill Lane, West Wratting, Cambridgeshire
title: Shug Monkey of Slough Hill Lane

desc: A small metal saucer about 18 inches across was reportedly found on moorland between Silpho and Hackness, containing thin copper sheets engraved with symbols. Its origin was never established and it is widely regarded as a hoax.
title: Silpho Moor saucer with copper scrolls

desc: Riders reported something like a microlight striking the summit mast and spiralling down in smoke, triggering a large search with an RAF helicopter. Nothing was found and no aircraft was missing.
title: Snaefell mast mystery crash

desc: A fireman's photograph of his daughter on the marshes showed a white-suited figure behind her that he believed was a spaceman. Later analysis concluded it was most likely his wife seen from behind.
source: Wikipedia – List of reported UFO sightings
title: Solway Firth 'spaceman' photo

desc: Footsteps have been reported on the stairs to the footbridge, along with cries and screams.
place: South Stack Lighthouse, near Holyhead, Anglesey
title: South Stack Lighthouse footsteps

desc: A poltergeist is said to be active at the cliff-top lighthouse, which was investigated in the ninth series of Most Haunted.
place: South Stack Lighthouse, Holy Island, Anglesey
title: South Stack Lighthouse poltergeist

desc: A South Wales Police helicopter crew reported taking evasive action from a saucer-like object near MOD St Athan and pursued it towards the Bristol Channel. Nothing was seen on radar and no explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: South Wales police helicopter near-miss

desc: On Midsummer evening 1745, 26 witnesses saw troops and carriages march along the ridge for hours; no tracks were found next day. Mirage explanations have been offered.
title: Souther Fell spectral army

desc: George Spicer and his wife reported a long-necked animal crossing the road ahead of their car near the loch. Later researchers argued the account was coloured by the dinosaur scene in King Kong.
title: Spicers see creature cross road, Loch Ness

desc: In 1904 crowds gathered on William Henry Street after rumours of a 'Spring-heel Jack'; missiles were thrown at a house until the tenants left, though police found nothing. A leaping figure was also claimed on St Francis Xavier's church roof in 1888.
title: Spring-heeled Jack in Everton

desc: Olivia Lenox-Conyngham is said to haunt the house and is described as one of Ireland's best-documented ghosts.
title: Springhill House, Olivia

desc: A mother and daughter reported large orange balls, then a white ball with a shutter-like feature, a change in the sky's colour and a loud noise. A photo was claimed to show a figure.
title: Sproatley orange balls

desc: Adomnan's life of St Columba, written about a century later, tells of the saint driving off a water beast that had attacked a man in the River Ness. Sceptics see it as a standard hagiographic motif.
title: St Columba and the River Ness beast

desc: Eleanor Jourdain, later principal of St Hugh's, reported seeing a medieval prisoner being dragged along the road by a jeering crowd in period dress.
place: St Hugh's College, St Margaret's Road, Oxford
title: St Margaret's Road medieval prisoner

desc: Over Christmas 2003 a triangular craft was reported over the Stainburn bypass heading towards the Lake District, among several West Cumbria sightings including a red object and an orange ball. No explanation was given.
title: Stainburn bypass triangle

desc: A witness who said they had RAF experience first took the object for an aircraft about 8-10 miles away. It then changed direction at about 45 degrees and sped off, getting brighter as it went.
title: Star-like object turns sharply over Denbigh

desc: A maid who starved after being locked in a room haunts the stairs and shows herself only to men; mild poltergeist activity and screeches on the answerphone are also reported.
place: Bear and Billet, Lower Bridge Street, Chester
title: Starved maid of the Bear and Billet

desc: For weeks stones, bricks and potatoes rained down on the street after dark, one knocking off a constable's helmet. Police believed a human culprit was responsible.
title: Stone-throwing on Kirkland Street, St Helens

desc: Police logged a report of a silver-and-black animal about the size of a sheepdog with a broader dark stripe than a domestic cat would have.
title: Striped sheepdog-sized cat, Denbigh

desc: A huge decayed carcass, measured at 55 ft, washed ashore after a storm and was named as a new sea serpent species. Anatomists later concluded it was a decomposed basking shark.
title: Stronsay Beast carcass

desc: Sightings of a large wild cat began in 1964 and the press named it after Crondall and Munstead. Surrey Police reviewed 362 reported sightings between September 1964 and August 1966.
title: Surrey Puma

desc: A figure in old-fashioned clothing, believed to be the last keeper and nicknamed Raymond, is said to stand on the lantern balcony looking out to sea. A steel sculpture of him later stood there for a while.
place: Point of Ayr Lighthouse, Talacre, Flintshire
source: Myths, Legends & Oddities of North East Wales
title: Talacre lighthouse keeper Raymond

desc: At about 7pm a resident saw a brownish animal larger than a dog, with a long thin tail, run into a field. A Puma Watch volunteer later found several sets of large paw prints at the spot.
title: Tawny cat and paw prints at Mynydd Isa

desc: Since the 1920s people have reported a dinosaur-like creature in Wales's largest natural lake. A Japanese film crew with a mini-submarine found nothing in the 1990s, and a park warden puts the disturbances down to fish, gas bubbles or otters.
title: Teggie, the Llyn Tegid monster

desc: Soldiers on fire picket filmed 13 lights over the barracks on a phone. A local landlord said they were Chinese lanterns from a wedding and the MoD accepted that.
source: The National Archives – UFO files highlights (2013)
title: Tern Hill barracks lights

desc: During the 1909 'mystery airship' wave a cyclist reported a silent airship-like craft about 400 ft long; another was reported the same day at Wroxham. No explanation was established.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Tharston 'scareship' airship

desc: Thrown objects and rearranged furniture at a cottage were followed by messages appearing on a BBC Micro computer, said to come from several spirits. The case was widely investigated.
title: The Dodleston messages

desc: Ambulance crews blamed footsteps, broken windows and doors that unlocked themselves on 'the Sarge', a policeman killed when his patrol wagon hit a bollard.
title: 'The Sarge' at the Woolton ambulance centre

desc: A six-year-old girl vanished from Bold Place behind the ruined church and was found holding the hand of a man in Victorian dress; she said an old woman in a shawl had led her inside. Researched by Tom Slemen.
place: Bold Place, behind St Luke's Church, Liverpool
title: The St Luke's abduction

desc: Robert Kenneth Wilson's famous long-necked photo appeared in the Daily Mail in April 1934. In 1991 one of those involved admitted it showed a toy submarine fitted with a model head and neck.
title: The 'Surgeon's Photograph' hoax

desc: Locals reported a dog-like animal about 60cm tall with a fox-like tail but an Alsatian look roaming the forest.
title: The Thing of Delamere

desc: A police officer reported a rotating object that was also picked up on air traffic radar. The radar return was put down to St Botolph's Church in Boston and the visual sighting to a celestial object.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: The Wash rotating object

desc: Nandor Fodor investigated disturbances around Mrs Forbes in 1938 and concluded they were psychological in origin and partly fraudulent.
title: Thornton Heath Poltergeist

desc: A caller told police they had seen a massive black puma-like cat in a field opposite a house. The police log describes it as tiger-sized, and officers investigated.
title: Tiger-sized black cat at Penmachno

desc: Aeronautical engineer Tim Dinsdale filmed a dark hump leaving a wake; a 1966 RAF analysis called it probably animate, but later work suggests a boat in poor light.
title: Tim Dinsdale's hump film, Loch Ness

desc: A woman testing a new phone camera later found one shot appeared to show a tiny grey alien-like figure walking along the road.
title: Tiny grey figure photographed, Balker Drive

desc: The manager says a glass was thrown at him in an empty upstairs room. He and about six colleagues saw a figure hanging from a ceiling on the CCTV monitor that was gone when they checked. Staff blame a projectionist who died in a 1940s fire, and Most Haunted filmed there.
place: The Tivoli, Brunswick Road, Buckley, Flintshire
title: Tivoli Buckley glass thrown and CCTV figure

desc: A police officer saw a domed object over the road and lost time. Later hypnosis sessions described an abduction.
title: Alan Godfrey abduction

desc: A grey monk heard speaking old English was seen several times in the 1970s. On Halloween 2003 children offered him their sweet bag and he is said to have eaten the contents, wrappers and all.
title: Trick-or-treating monk at Chester Cathedral

desc: A fisherman described an animal with a bull-sized head, walrus-like tusks and a large back fin swimming towards him before diving. A 1958 student 'monster' on the lough was a deliberate Rag Week hoax.
place: Antrim Bay, Lough Neagh, Co. Antrim
title: Tusked creature in Antrim Bay, Lough Neagh

desc: Two Australian visitors near the Glen Garry viewpoint saw a twin-humped serpent-like shape about 100 m offshore for around ten seconds.
title: Twin-humped serpent, Loch Garry

desc: Within five minutes of each other, a red-and-green star-like object was seen over Caernarfon and a large blue glowing object that turned green, broke up and left smoke was seen over Amlwch. Both appear in the government's 2001 UFO report.
title: Twin sightings over Caernarfon and Amlwch

desc: A holidaymaker in one car saw a Labrador-sized black cat with a very long, thick tail in a roadside field. A friend in the car behind independently reported seeing it at the same spot.
title: Two cars see long-tailed cat near Llanfechell

desc: A large bright orange light turned white and then vanished quickly without any sound. No explanation was given.
title: Tywyn orange-to-white light

desc: In the late 1990s a cyclist looked up at the bridge and saw two or three people in old-fashioned clothes who then vanished. Condemned prisoners once crossed it to chapel.
place: Bridge of Sighs, Northgate Street, Chester
title: Vanishing figures on the Bridge of Sighs

desc: In early 1965 a driver on the Southport-Ormskirk road saw an elderly man in a flat cap sitting in the back of his Mini, who had gone when he leapt out. Years later another man described the same thing at the same bridge.
title: Vanishing passenger on Halsall Moss

desc: Children's crying and laughter are heard on the stairs, a ghost girl is said to push visitors and Lady Daresbury is said to haunt her rooms.
title: Walton Hall, Warrington

desc: Strange sounds and lights over the town drew sky-watchers to Cradle Hill for years.
title: The Warminster Thing

desc: Elsie Oakensen reported dumbbell-shaped lights above the road, her car cutting out, and about 15 minutes she could not account for. No explanation was given.
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: Weedon Bec dumbbell lights and lost time

desc: Radar at West Freugh tracked a large stationary target at about 50,000 ft that then climbed sharply and turned at speed. No explanation was published.
place: RAF West Freugh, Dumfries and Galloway
source: Wikipedia – UFO sightings in the United Kingdom
title: West Freugh radar object

desc: A member of the public reported a fluorescent green saucer appearing to harass an aircraft near Prestwick. No explanation was given.
title: West Kilbride green saucer

desc: A woman in white is said to haunt the area around the Wylfa nuclear power station on Anglesey's north coast.
title: White lady near Wylfa

desc: A bride said to have died after her husband's killing on their wedding night haunts the walls; in 1922 a medical officer reported being pushed downstairs by a robed young woman.
title: White Lady of Charles Fort

desc: A woman in a white dress is said to walk alone along the promenade and coast path between Prestatyn and Rhyl. Legend says she drowned herself in the sea.
place: Prestatyn seafront near the Nova, Denbighshire
title: White Lady of Prestatyn promenade

desc: Two walkers heading for Frodsham met a white lady who stared at them for minutes and then floated up into the trees.
place: Delamere Forest near Delamere Station, Delamere
title: White lady rising into the trees, Delamere

desc: At 2.30pm a round, bright white object hovered and then moved slowly and silently from south-west to north-east near Holyhead.
title: White sphere drifts over Holyhead

desc: Six people at the clubhouse saw a silent round light several feet across cross the sky, puff smoke, accelerate and drop onto the course. Searches found nothing.
title: Whitehaven golf course light

desc: The gaol, used from 1702 to 1924, is said to be haunted by inmates who died there, many during the Famine.
title: Wicklow Gaol

desc: A 17-year-old saw a black spherical craft with an antenna fly overhead. Ufologist Jenny Randles speculated it could have been a lost Merseyside Police drone.
title: Widnes black sphere with antenna

desc: In December 1684 William Batt was reportedly seen arriving home at dusk and left a bloody footprint, on the day he was killed in London.
title: William Batt, Oakwell Hall

desc: A caller reported a stationary red light to the east watched for 20 minutes after midnight. Cheshire Police established it was a light on a crane.
title: Wilmslow red light (crane)

desc: Two police officers on patrol reported watching an unidentified object pass over the city. No explanation was recorded.
title: Wincolmlee police patrol UFO

desc: Investigators report unease and a growl attributed to a Freemason's spirit, and a pregnant woman who lost her baby in a fall is said to walk the stairs.
place: Woolton Hall, Speke Road, Woolton, Liverpool
title: Woolton Hall stair ghost
